From 13a9d08c296228d18289de60b83792c586e1d073 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Aug 2022 18:00:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] net: lan966x: improve error handle in
 lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame()

Don't just print a warning.  Clean up and return an error as well.

Fixes: c8349639324a ("net: lan966x: Add FDMA functionality")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Horatiu Vultur <horatiu.vultur@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/YwjgDm/SVd5c1tQU@kili
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
index 6dea7f8c1481..51f8a0816377 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c
@@ -425,7 +425,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 	lan966x_ifh_get_src_port(skb->data, &src_port);
 	lan966x_ifh_get_timestamp(skb->data, &timestamp);
 
-	WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
+	if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
+		goto free_skb;
 
 	skb->dev = lan966x->ports[src_port]->dev;
 	skb_pull(skb, IFH_LEN * sizeof(u32));
@@ -449,6 +450,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame(struct lan966x_rx *rx)
 
 	return skb;
 
+free_skb:
+	kfree_skb(skb);
 unmap_page:
 	dma_unmap_page(lan966x->dev, (dma_addr_t)db->dataptr,
 		       FDMA_DCB_STATUS_BLOCKL(db->status),
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/microchip/lan966x/lan966x_fdma.c`**
1. **Line Modification**: The original line that used `WARN_ON` to check if `src_port` is greater than or equal to `lan966x->num_phys_ports` has been modified. Instead of just issuing a warning, it now checks the condition and, if true, jumps to a cleanup label (`free_skb`).
2. **Error Handling**: A new label `free_skb` has been added, which calls `kfree_skb(skb)` to free the socket buffer (`skb`) before exiting the function. This ensures that if an error is detected, the allocated resources are properly cleaned up.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification enhances the error handling in the `lan966x_fdma_rx_get_frame` function. Previously, the function would only print a warning if the `src_port` was invalid, potentially leading to resource leaks if the function continued executing. The new implementation not only warns about the invalid condition but also ensures that the allocated socket buffer is freed before returning, thus improving the robustness of the error handling in the function. This change is directly related to the previous functionality added in the commit referenced by the `Fixes` tag, indicating that it addresses a flaw in the error management introduced earlier.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports);
```
```c
skb = build_skb(page_address(page), PAGE_SIZE << rx->page_order);
```
```c
dma_unmap_single(lan966x->dev, (dma_addr_t)db->dataptr, FDMA_DCB_STATUS_BLOCKL(db->status), DMA_FROM_DEVICE);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `WARN_ON` statement only logs a warning when `src_port` is invalid (i.e., greater than or equal to `num_phys_ports`), but it does not handle the error condition properly. This can lead to resource leaks since the allocated `skb` and other resources may not be cleaned up, resulting in potential memory exhaustion or undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (WARN_ON(src_port >= lan966x->num_phys_ports))
    goto free_skb;
```
```c
free_skb:
    kfree_skb(skb);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a conditional check that, upon detecting an invalid `src_port`, jumps to the `free_skb` label to properly free the allocated `skb` before returning `NULL`. This ensures that resources are cleaned up correctly, preventing memory leaks and ensuring stable behavior in error conditions.
